rationale: The frozen source leaves status blank for every positive elapsed-day value and sets NEW at zero. The blank lines suggest a possible missing SLA classification rule, but neither the source nor the supplied clause establishes OK/LATE as the required status interface. Clause 65(8) requires a CKYCR update within seven days; classification alone cannot establish that an update occurred. Revise the intended behavior to a justified, limited elapsed-day classification claim and supply support for the proposed status conventions before inclusion.
scope_judgment: Lines 22–26 are blank lines inside 2000-CHECK-SLA immediately before the existing zero-day NEW rule. They form a plausible local insertion scope for classification, with the zero-day rule preserved outside that scope. The supplied source has no registry transmission or completion tracking, so this scope does not substantiate the stated regulatory compliance outcome.
intended_fixture_judgment: The eight-day fixture tests the first day beyond the inclusive seven-day deadline, but its LATE expectation is an unsupported proposed convention. Together with the seven-day fixture it covers the threshold boundary for classification. It does not observe a CKYCR update, its receipt timestamp, or its completion time and cannot prove the stated intended regulatory behavior.
regression_fixture_judgment: The zero-day NEW expectation is grounded in the existing source and is a useful unaffected regression. The one-day and seven-day OK expectations are new behavior: the frozen source currently leaves the status blank for both. They should be relabeled as intended classification fixtures rather than preservation of existing valid outcomes. The finite fixtures do not establish general equivalence outside the allowlisted locus or cover repeated paragraph invocation with an existing status.
capability_judgment: The supplied capability evidence identifies GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 and support for batch execution, which fits this simple standalone program and direct paragraph fixtures. It explicitly states that case checks have not been executed; no fixture pass is established. The supported proof scope is finite execution observations, with no complete semantic equivalence proof. Even successful execution of these fixtures would establish only the observed status classifications.
duplicate_source_judgment: Preselection before detector results provides a defensible reason to retain repeated bundles conditionally, provided the stated all-reviewer approval requirement is met. Dependence must remain disclosed through source_bundle_group, counts of cases and distinct bundles, and the prohibition on independent-case interval claims. This packet alone cannot establish approval of other members of the dependent group.
unresolved_issues: The OK/LATE status conventions lack supporting interface evidence.
The stated intended behavior overclaims regulatory compliance from status classification.
The one-day and seven-day fixtures are mislabeled as existing-behavior regressions.
No case execution results are supplied.
Repeated-source retention remains conditional on all required reviewer approvals and disclosed dependence.
